reason: The cited evidence supports the general use of descriptors like misfit volumes and stacking fault energies for strength/ductility models (E1) and notes the potential of ML for HEAs (E2, E3), but no evidence is provided for the specific claim that reduced-order simulations can capture the complex hierarchical heterostructure of HfNbTiVAl10, nor for the predicted accuracy and efficiency gains for fracture toughness, which E1 states is mostly out of reach for DFT. The key premises regarding descriptor extraction from the specific heterostructure and the model's performance are thus largely unsupp
premises: Reduced-order descriptors (misfit volume, local elastic moduli, stacking fault and surface energies) can be extracted from scale-bridging simulations of the hierarchical heterostructure.
These descriptors capture the influence of spatially resolved chemical and microstructural fluctuations on mechanical behavior.
An ML model can learn non-linear relationships between these descriptors and macroscopic Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
This hybrid approach will be significantly more efficient than full-scale CALPHAD or ab initio methods.
The approach will achieve high accuracy (errors below 5-10%) for these properties.
